paragraphs.text: A [red tea](red:definition) from Taiwan, made in 2023 and recorded as competition grade. Red tea is what English calls black tea: the leaf is fully oxidised, left after rolling until its own enzymes turn it from green to reddish brown, a step the Chinese trade calls fermentation. Taiwan’s [red tea](red:history) dates from the Japanese period, when it was first grown at Yuchi near Sun Moon Lake.

Red tea has [no tradition of ageing](red:ageing). Sealed, it keeps its quality for about a year and a half to three years, and at three years this tea is at the far end of that span, so it is one to drink now rather than keep.

brewing.text: Red tea takes water near the boil, about 90 to 100°C; hotter water draws out its aroma and flavour more fully, but its bitterness faster too. In a pot or mug, use about a rounded spoon of leaf for each cup and steep three to five minutes, less for broken leaf and a little less, and a little cooler, for a light, delicate tea. Left too long, it turns bitter and drying, because time and heat pull more tannins from the leaf.

notice.text: A sweet cup, often with honey, floral or fruity notes, malt in many, and a brisk strength in the stronger teas. The liquor runs red, bright to deep.
